input: A traditional taverna in Thessaloniki called To Steki. Menu, hours, a map, and a phone number: 2310 555 123.
why: A phone number given verbatim must appear verbatim AND be tappable — the whole point on mobile.

input: A law firm site. Serious, no animation at all, no gradients.
why: An explicit prohibition is the easiest instruction to verify and the most common one ignored.

input: A photographer's portfolio. I want a dark background.
why: 'Dark background' is a colour instruction that must survive into the CSS.

input: A bakery landing page with a contact form that emails me.
why: A form without an email field cannot do the one thing it was asked for.

input: A one-page site for a plumber in Patras. Include a section titled 'Emergency Callout'.
why: A named section is a literal string; its absence is unambiguous non-compliance.

input: Portfolio site. Use the font Poppins.
why: A named font must be both referenced and actually loaded, or it renders as fallback.

input: A site for a Greek olive oil producer. Text in Greek.
why: Content language and the lang attribute must agree or screen readers and SEO both break.

input: A gym site. Do NOT include any testimonials.
why: The banned generic shape includes a testimonial band; an explicit ban tests whether the default wins.

input: A dentist's site with opening hours Mon-Fri 9-5, Sat 9-1, closed Sunday.
why: Structured factual data given in the brief must not be paraphrased into something different.

input: A minimal single-column site for a poet. No images.
why: 'No images' is checkable exactly, and the image pipeline is eager by default.

input: A landing page for a SaaS product. Include a pricing table with three tiers: Free, Pro 19, Business 49.
why: Prices are numbers a visitor acts on; a wrong one is a commercial error.

input: A wedding photographer's site. Make the hero a full-bleed photo.
why: An explicit hero pattern must override whatever the per-site draw chose.

input: A car repair shop site. Include a Google Maps link to Leoforos Alexandras 12, Athens.
why: An address given verbatim must appear and be linked, not summarised.

input: A page for my consultancy. Absolutely no stock photos of people in offices.
why: A negative content instruction about imagery, which the placeholder pipeline is prone to violate.

input: A charity site. It must be accessible: every image needs alt text.
why: An img without alt is a mechanical accessibility failure, and the check must also pass a page with no images at all.

input: A site for a barbershop. Single page, no navigation menu.
why: 'No navigation' contradicts the default structure and tests instruction precedence.

input: A tutoring site. Include exactly two call-to-action buttons, both saying 'Book a lesson'.
why: Exact button copy is what a user will look for; paraphrasing it is a silent rewrite.

input: A site with no external resources whatsoever. Everything inline.
why: The prompt permits Google Fonts as an exception; an explicit ban must beat the exception.

input: A restaurant site. The owner's name is Γιώργος Παπαδόπουλος — spell it exactly.
why: Non-Latin proper nouns are where transliteration silently corrupts someone's name.

input: A site for a startup. Do not invent any statistics or customer numbers.
why: Invented social proof is a legal and trust problem, and it is the generator's most persistent habit.

input: A florist's site in Larissa with a section for weddings and one for funerals.
why: Two named sections, one of which a model may soften or drop for tone reasons.

input: A page that works with JavaScript disabled.
why: A scroll-reveal that starts at opacity 0 leaves a blank page with JS off — invisible in every source gate.
